options.B: Interest paid on debentures
options.C: Income tax paid
options.D: All of the above

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Over-absorption of works overhead.

Over-absorption means the cost accounts charged more overhead than was actually incurred, so costing profit is understated and the excess must be added back. Interest paid on debentures and income tax are purely financial expenses charged only in the financial accounts, so they are deducted.

case_facts_html:
Anantam Ltd. operates a batch costing system fully integrated with its financial accounts. The following information relates to the month of June 2026:

Opening balances: Stores Ledger Control Account ₹40,000; Work-in-Process Control Account ₹32,000; Finished Goods Control Account ₹56,000; prepaid production overheads brought forward from the previous month ₹4,000.

Transactions during the month: materials purchased ₹1,20,000; materials issued to production ₹48,000; materials issued to factory maintenance ₹6,000; materials transferred between batches ₹8,000; wages paid to direct workers ₹40,000; wages paid to indirect workers ₹9,000; direct wages charged to batches ₹34,000; recorded non-productive time of direct workers ₹6,000; selling and distribution overheads incurred ₹10,000; other production overheads incurred ₹18,000; sales ₹1,60,000; cost of finished goods sold ₹1,28,000; cost of goods completed and transferred into finished goods during the month ₹1,04,000; physical value of work-in-process at the end of the month ₹62,000.

The production overhead absorption rate is 150% of direct wages charged to work-in-process.
question_html: What is the profit shown by the Costing Profit and Loss Account of Anantam Ltd. for June 2026?
answer_html:
Answer: (D) ₹31,000.

Debits: cost of finished goods sold ₹1,28,000 + selling and distribution overheads ₹10,000 = ₹1,38,000. Credits: sales ₹1,60,000 + production overhead over-absorbed ₹8,000 + work-in-process stock gain ₹1,000 = ₹1,69,000. Profit = ₹31,000. The stock gain of ₹1,000 arises because the physical value of ₹62,000 exceeds the book balance of ₹61,000 (₹32,000 + ₹48,000 + ₹34,000 + ₹51,000 - ₹1,04,000). Option (A) omits both the over-absorption and the stock gain.
